# Unequal homothetic triangle pairs can fall below the sum of ordinary depths

Let `T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}` and `V=|T|=1/2`. For bodies
`A,B` and a common point `y`, define

    p_AB(y)=inf_(u!=0,t in R)
        [ |A cap {u.x>=u.y+t}|+|B cap {u.x>=u.y-t}| ].

The proposed inequality

    p_AB(y) >= f_A(y)+f_B(y)

is false even when `A` and `B` are positive homothets about the same
triangle vertex, and `y` is the centroid of the larger
triangle and an interior point of the smaller one. No translation or
numerical optimization is needed.

## 1. A rational counterexample with one shared normal

Take

    A=T,       B=(4/3)T,       y=(4/9,4/9).

The point lies strictly inside both triangles and is the centroid of
`B`. Their absolute ordinary depths are exactly

    f_A(y)=16V/81,       f_B(y)=64V/81,
    f_A(y)+f_B(y)=80V/81.                                   (1)

For the ONE common normal `u=(1,1)` and shift `t=-4/9`, the two
thresholds are respectively `4/9` and `4/3`. The first cap removes a
corner triangle of area `(4/9)^2 V`; the second is the supporting top
edge of `B`, of zero two-dimensional volume. Consequently

    p_AB(y) <= (1-16/81)V+0=65V/81
              =f_A(y)+f_B(y)-5V/27.                          (2)

Supporting boundaries are not essential. For the same normal and
shift `t=-1/3`, the thresholds are `5/9` and `11/9`, both strictly
between zero and the respective triangle heights. Their areas are

    |A cap {x1+x2>=5/9}|=56V/81,
    |B cap {x1+x2>=11/9}|=23V/81.

Their sum is `79V/81<80V/81`. Thus two strictly proper closed cuts
already certify the failure. Every boundary line has zero area.
Neither (2) nor the proper-cut certificate is claimed to equal the
fully optimized paired cost.

## 2. Why both ordinary depths are certified against all normals

For every point of any triangle, if its barycentric coordinates sorted
in decreasing order are `A0>=B0>=C0`, its ordinary depth is exactly

    4 B0 C0 times the triangle's area.                        (3)

Here is a self-contained all-orientation justification. Move a containing
cap until its boundary passes through the point. A cap containing one
vertex and intersecting its two incident edges at parameters `s,t` has
area fraction `st`, with through-point relation
`lambda_j/s+lambda_k/t=1`. AM--GM gives
`st>=4 lambda_j lambda_k>=4B0C0`. Boundary vertices are included by
allowing an intercept to equal one.

For a cap containing two vertices, its complement is a corner triangle
at the excluded vertex `k`. Write the two complementary intercepts
as `s,t`. Setting `v=lambda_i/s`, the through-point relation gives
`lambda_i<=v<=1-lambda_j` and complementary fraction
`lambda_i lambda_j/[v(1-v)]`. The concave quadratic denominator has
its minimum at an endpoint of this interval. The captured fraction is
therefore at least

    min{lambda_k/(1-lambda_i),lambda_k/(1-lambda_j)}
       >= C0/(A0+C0) >=4B0C0.

The last inequality is `4B0(1-B0)<=1`. Conversely, a corner cap at
a largest-coordinate vertex with intercepts `2B0,2C0` is valid since
`B0<=1/2`, passes through the point, and has fraction `4B0C0`.
Boundary points follow from a zero-area supporting cap. This proves
(3), also established in the preceding all-point identical-triangle
pair theorem; no restriction to diagonal or coordinate normals occurs.

For the smaller triangle in Section 1 the barycentric coordinates are
`(1/9,4/9,4/9)`, so (3) gives `16V/81`. One matching ordinary cap
is `4x1+3x2>=28/9`. For the larger triangle all three barycentric
coordinates are `1/3`; its area is `(16/9)V`, so (3) gives
`(4/9)(16/9)V=64V/81`. This verifies (1) exactly.

## 3. A full diagonal family of strict counterexamples

Let

    0<r<s<3r/2,      2s/3<=L<r,
    A=rT,           B=sT,          y=(L/2,L/2).

The point is interior to both triangles. The two smallest scaled
barycentric coordinates are `r-L,L/2` for `A` and `s-L,L/2`
for `B`. Formula (3), with the actual areas `r^2V,s^2V`, gives

    f_A(y)=2VL(r-L),       f_B(y)=2VL(s-L).                   (4)

Use `u=(1,1)` and `t=L-s`. The first threshold is `2L-s`, strictly
between zero and `r`; the second is the supporting threshold `s`.
Their total cost is

    V[r^2-(2L-s)^2].

Its strict shortfall from the sum in (4) is exactly

    Delta V,       Delta=(s-r)(r+s-2L)>0.                    (5)

There is also a uniform explicit proper-cut repair. Replace the second
threshold `s` by `s-epsilon` and the first by `2L-s+epsilon`, where
`epsilon=Delta/(8s)`. Both are proper: `epsilon<r+s-2L` and
`epsilon<s`. Their cost increases from the supporting-cap expression
by

    4(s-L)epsilon-2epsilon^2 <=4s epsilon=Delta/2.

Thus every member of this family admits two proper cuts whose total
is still at least `Delta V/2` below `f_A(y)+f_B(y)`.

At `L=2s/3`, the point is the centroid of the larger triangle. The
supporting-cap certificate divided by the sum of ordinary depths is

    (3r+s)/(4s).

As `s/r` increases to `3/2` from below, this ratio tends to `3/4`,
while the common point remains interior to the smaller triangle at
every finite step. Therefore any universal factor `c` in a bound
`p_AB(y)>=c[f_A(y)+f_B(y)]` on this class must satisfy `c<=3/4`.
No matching lower bound or optimality of `3/4` is asserted.

## 4. Scope

The exact all-point identical-triangle identity does not extend to
unequal positive homothetic scales. The lower-diagonal equal-copy
payment remains consistent: the counterexamples lie beyond the
smaller triangle's centroid, so its centered inscribed-copy hypothesis
does not hold. The examples preserve a single common normal and one
pair of opposite shifts throughout.

This is an auxiliary paired-cost counterexample. It does not specify
all the fibers of an actual three-layer convex source, does not claim
an OC failure, and supplies no counterexample for homothetic triangles
when the point is restricted to the common lower-diagonal region.

The exact verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_unequal_triangle_pair_below_ordinary_sum.py`
checks the areas, matching ordinary caps, the two proper cuts, and
the strict family identities using rational arithmetic.
